newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money rates still high, waiting for New Year.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money rates still high, waiting for New Year.

text.p: Most Dutch money market rates held on to their pre-Christmas levels on Friday, with call money bid even higher (up to 3.18 percent) in a deadly quiet market.
Dealers say most players have closed their books and will not return to the market before the new year.

Some activity was seen in over the year-end deposits (one- week deposits), which were bid between 3.25 and 3.31, above all other money market rates. One-week deposits were said to change hands at 3.375.
German money market deals done today will settle on January 2, which has caused rates to come down quite sharply since the 24th, and Dutch money market rates are expected to do the same on January 2.
Trades done today on the Dutch money market still settle in 1996.
Dealers expect the new special advances pact announced this afternoon to be at an unchanged rate of 2.50 percent, but say the duration could be very short which might give some sparkle to the market.
